records.title: Ray: A Distributed Framework for Emerging AI Applications
records.reason: Ray is a general-purpose distributed framework for interactive AI applications. The paper's conclusion notes a training/serving/simulation loop, but the motivating applications and reported evaluation focus on reinforcement-learning workloads and distributed task throughput (up to 1.8 million tasks/s), not LLM inference or LLM-serving efficiency. General framework applicability alone does not establish the required LLM-inference focus, so this is unrelated to the assigned scope.

records.title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism
records.reason: The primary source explicitly presents an intra-layer model-parallel method for training large Transformer models; experiments train models up to 8.3B parameters using 512 NVIDIA V100 GPUs (§1, §3-5). Its 15.1 PFLOP/s application throughput and 76% scaling efficiency describe distributed training. The conclusion's future work remains larger-scale pretraining and optimizer memory efficiency (§6). No inference-time efficiency method or evaluation is presented in the reviewed paper.

records.title: Blockwise Self-Attention for Long Document Understanding
records.reason: BlockBERT replaces dense self-attention with blockwise sparse attention and reports 27.8% lower inference time than RoBERTa at batch 8 and sequence length 1,024, with comparable QA accuracy. The evidence is for encoder-only BERT-family models and long-document QA rather than decoder-only LLM generation or serving. The attention idea is adjacent and potentially transferable, but the evaluated workload is outside core LLM inference, so it is retained as borderline.

records.title: LightSeq: A High Performance Inference Library for Sequence Processing and Generation

records.title: ZeroQuant: Efficient and Affordable Post-Training Quantization for Large-Scale Transformers
records.reason: ZeroQuant is an end-to-end quantization and inference pipeline combining hardware-friendly weight/activation quantization, affordable layerwise distillation and backend support to reduce quantization overhead. It reports INT8 inference gains up to 5.19x on BERT, 3.67x on GPT-J-6B, and reduced GPT-NeoX-20B latency from 65 ms to 25 ms while reducing inference GPUs from two to one. This directly optimizes model serving performance and memory.

records.title: SparseGPT: Massive Language Models Can be Accurately Pruned in One-Shot

It also covers hardware-friendly 2:4 and 4:8 sparsity and sparsity-plus-quantization. This is model compression intended to lower LLM inference resource cost.

records.title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models
records.reason: Mixture-of-Depths learns a router that skips transformer blocks for selected tokens, reducing per-forward-pass FLOPs. While substantial experiments measure training/isoFLOP behavior, the primary paper verifies autoregressive sampling and supports inference-time execution, so it is relevant to adaptive inference computation.

records.title: SpinQuant: LLM Quantization with Learned Rotations
records.reason: SpinQuant learns rotations that improve post-training quantization of LLM weights, activations and KV cache. The paper evaluates 4-bit quantization across LLMs and states that one variant merges learned rotations into weights before inference; the online Hadamard variant adds approximately 8% network latency. It directly studies inference-time memory/latency versus quantization accuracy.

records.title: Towards Efficient Mixture of Experts: A Holistic Study of Compression Techniques
records.reason: The paper evaluates Layer Drop, Block Drop, expert quantization, and pruning for MoE inference efficiency. On Mixtral-8x7B, combined trimming and quantization are reported to provide up to 6.05x speedup at 20.0 GB memory, a 77.1% reduction, while retaining over 92% of original performance. Its objective and measured results directly concern MoE inference computation and memory.

records.title: Post-Training Sparse Attention with Double Sparsity
records.reason: Double Sparsity reduces LLM inference KV-cache access using token and channel sparsity, with optional offloading. The primary paper evaluates Llama-2-7B and other LLMs, reporting a minimum 1.3x throughput gain and near-2x in some tested conditions; the offload variant reports 4–8x over FlexGen on regular workloads and up to 16x on 64K–256K long sequences. This is directly inference-time attention and memory optimization.

records.title: Dynamic Depth Decoding: Faster Speculative Decoding for LLMs
records.reason: Dynamic Depth Decoding modifies EAGLE-2 by choosing draft-tree depth dynamically. The primary paper describes speculative decoding as lossless because target-model verification preserves the output, and reports an average 3.16× speedup with a 44% increase over EAGLE's average speedup across its experiments. This is directly about accelerating LLM autoregressive inference.

records.title: No Request Left Behind: Tackling Heterogeneity in Long-Context LLM Inference with Medha
records.reason: Medha combines preemptive chunked prefills, Stream Pipeline Parallelism, KV-Cache Parallelism, dynamic batch packing and a length-aware scheduler for heterogeneous long-context inference. On stated workloads it reports 5.7× throughput over state-of-the-art non-preemptive systems and up to 30× lower median latency and 174× lower P99 latency. Direct serving optimization.

records.title: AMUSD: Asynchronous Multi-Device Speculative Decoding for LLM Acceleration
records.reason: AMUSD lets draft and verify models run continuously and asynchronously on separate devices, with rollback handling to preserve consistency. Its evaluation uses Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-3.2-1B across several benchmarks; it reports up to 1.96× speedup over autoregressive decoding and identical output quality, including improved utilization through concurrent GPU execution. This directly targets LLM decoding latency and throughput.

records.title: Context Parallelism for Scalable Million-Token Inference
records.reason: The paper presents context parallelism for long-context LLM inference, including lossless pass-KV and pass-Q ring-attention variants for full prefill, partial prefill and decoding. It reports near-linear scaling to 128 H100 GPUs; a 1M-token prefill for Llama 3 405B in 77 seconds with 93% parallelization efficiency and 63% FLOPS utilization, and 128K prefill in 3.8 seconds. This directly addresses inference scalability and latency.

records.title: SuffixDecoding: Extreme Speculative Decoding for Emerging AI Applications
records.reason: The primary title differs from the worklist title, but the identity and paper match. records.title: ReMoE: Fully Differentiable Mixture-of-Experts with ReLU Routing
records.reason: ReMoE replaces TopK+Softmax with differentiable ReLU routing and dynamically allocates experts. Its central motivation and experiments focus on differentiability and training scalability; it reports inference throughput within −2.29% to +3.89% of conventional TopK MoE, i.e. roughly comparable speed rather than an inference-efficiency gain. Relevant MoE serving architecture, but evidence does not show inference reduction as its primary objective.

records.title: Efficiently Serving Large Multimodal Models Using EPD Disaggregation
records.reason: EPD Disaggregation separates multimodal encoding, LLM prefill and decode onto dedicated resources and adds media-token caching, within-request encoder parallelism, allocation and role switching. This directly targets multimodal LLM inference serving.

records.title: KVTuner: Sensitivity-Aware Layer-Wise Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization for Efficient and Nearly Lossless LLM Inference

records.reason: KernelBench measures whether LLMs can generate correct and fast GPU kernels for a broad set of ML workloads. records.title: Block Diffusion: Interpolating Between Autoregressive and Diffusion Language Models
records.reason: Block Diffusion introduces an LLM generation procedure that caches keys/values between blocks and samples tokens in parallel within a block, addressing inference efficiency and arbitrary-length generation. The paper also provides an optimized block-attention implementation reporting about 15% faster model forward pass than replacing the FlashAttention kernel in its tested A5000 setup. Although the work includes a training method and does not report end-to-end serving throughput, the generation algorithm and measured attention execution are within LLM inference scope.

records.title: MiLo: Efficient Quantized MoE Inference with Mixture of Low-Rank Compensators
records.reason: MiLo augments low-bit quantized MoE weights with low-rank compensators to recover accuracy and implements Tensor Core-friendly W3A16 GEMM kernels to turn compression into measured inference latency gains. On Mixtral 8×7B with an A100, its backend reports 1.2× speedup at batch size 1 and 1.26× at larger batches against MARLIN. This directly reduces MoE inference memory and latency.

records.title: On Evaluating Performance of LLM Inference Systems
records.reason: This paper directly studies how LLM inference serving systems should be evaluated: it identifies baseline fairness, workload selection, latency/SLO and metric-design pitfalls, then demonstrates the issues through speculative decoding. It contributes an evaluation checklist and empirical analysis rather than an inference-serving mechanism or an efficiency improvement itself. Retained as borderline because its object is LLM inference-system performance and reproducibility, while its contribution is methodological evaluation rather than system optimization.

records.title: Huawei Cloud Model-as-a-Service on the CloudMatrix384 SuperPod
records.reason: This paper describes xDeepServe, Huawei Cloud's production Model-as-a-Service system for large MoE LLMs on CloudMatrix384. It combines decentralized data-parallel serving, expert load balancing, prefill/decode and Transformerless disaggregation, and a memory-semantic communication layer. The paper reports peak decoding of 2,400 tokens/s per Ascend 910C chip at about 50 ms TPOT, and a representative production setup with 900 ms TTFT and 34.8 ms average TPOT. It directly documents LLM inference system design and measurements.
